category_title: Disruptive students who feel targeted and disrespected by authority figures
minimal_context: Kyle is coming into the classroom to take his seat and begin his daily classwork.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Everyone, please take your seats and start your classwork. Kyle, what happened between you and Mrs. W? If you have problems today, I will write your name on the board.

STUDENT: I just came into class and sat down. Why are you bringing that up?

TUTOR: I'm just letting you know. You're like Mrs. W's son.

STUDENT: That joke is weird. You're offending me.

TUTOR: That is enough talking back. I am putting your name on the board right now.

STUDENT: (Gets loud) You started making me mad! When I'm doing my work and someone is bothering me, I'm the one that then gets in trouble! (Erases his name from the board when the teacher turns to look at the rest of the class)

options.A: Teach a replacement behavior for the student to use when he feels bothered during classwork.
options.B: Guide the student through short practices focusing on breath awareness, belly breathing, and body awareness.
options.C: Allow the student to tell his side of the story instead of immediately assigning a consequence.
options.D: Provide the student with detailed instruction for each specific element of the daily classwork.
